classified.text: Riders shall be able to submit a ride request specifying pickup and drop‑off locations, desired vehicle type, and payment method.
RideNow shall locate drivers within a 5‑kilometer radius and present the closest available driver to the rider.
The system shall match a rider with a driver in under 3 seconds after the request is received.
Drivers shall be able to toggle their availability status between online and offline.
An driver shall accept or reject a pending trip request within 30 seconds of notification.
The rider shall receive a real‑time map displaying the driver’s current location and estimated time of arrival.
Users can track the trip progress on a live map and view distance traveled, elapsed time, and current fare estimate.
The platform shall calculate the estimated fare using base rate, distance, duration, and any applicable surge multiplier.
Riders shall be able to confirm payment using a saved credit card, digital wallet, or cash option at the end of the trip.
After a trip is completed, the rider shall be prompted to rate the driver on a 1‑5 star scale and optionally leave written feedback.
Drivers shall be prompted to rate the rider on a 1‑5 star scale and may add comments after trip completion.
The system shall apply surge pricing automatically when demand exceeds supply in a defined geographic zone.
Administrators shall configure surge multipliers and define surge zones through an admin console.
Riders shall be able to cancel a pending request before a driver accepts without incurring a fee.
Riders shall be charged a cancellation fee if the request is cancelled after a driver has accepted.
Drivers shall be able to update their trip status to “arriving”, “in‑progress”, and “completed” which is reflected to the rider in real time.
The platform shall generate a digital receipt containing trip details, fare breakdown, and payment confirmation, and email it to the rider.
Drivers shall have access to an earnings dashboard showing completed trips, total earnings, and pending payouts.
RideNow shall scale elastically across multiple cloud regions to handle peak demand spikes without degradation of matching latency.
The service shall maintain an availability of 99.9 % measured on a monthly basis, with automatic failover to standby instances.
Real‑time location updates shall be delivered to riders and drivers within 1 second of change, supporting a smooth tracking experience.
All data in transit shall be encrypted using TLS 1.3, and sensitive data at rest shall be protected with AES‑256 encryption.
Access to administrative functions shall be restricted to authorized personnel through role‑based access control (RBAC).
The platform shall emit structured logs, metrics, and distributed traces to a centralized observability stack for monitoring and debugging.
Payment processing shall comply with PCI‑DSS requirements and shall not store raw card numbers on the platform.
Deployment pipelines shall support zero‑downtime rolling updates and automated rollback on health‑check failures.
